test_title: SSC CHSL Tier-1 2023: Official Paper (Held On: 10 Aug, 2023 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: In the central budget 2023-24, the term 'Amrit Peedhi' refers to:

options.text: children as the future of India

solution:
The correct answer is __**youth**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

**Union Budget 2023-24:-**

 
• It was presented by Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman on February 1, 2023.
 
• The budget had a strong focus on empowering the youth, especially the Amrit Peedhi, through education, skill development, and job creation.
 
• In the central budget 2023-24, **the term 'Amrit Peedhi' refers to the generation that will be responsible for building India in the next 25 years. It is a Hindi term that literally means 'Nectar Generation'.**
 
• The term was first used by Prime Minister Narendra Modi in 2021 to refer to the generation of Indians who will be born after the country's 75th anniversary of independence in 2022.
 
• This generation will be tasked with carrying India forward into its next phase of development, which is known as the 'Amrit Kaal' (Nectar Age).
 
• Some of the key highlights of the Union Budget 2023-24:
 
 
• **Education:**
 
 
• Establishment of a National Digital University to provide high-quality education to students across India.
 
• Increase in the number of Eklavya Model Residential Schools for tribal students.
 
• Launch of a new scheme to provide scholarships to students from Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes for studying abroad.
 
 
 
• **Skill development:**
 
 
• Launch of Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana 4.0 to skill lakhs of youth within the next three years.
 
• Setting up of 30 Skill India International Centres across different states to skill the youth for international opportunities.
 
 
 
• **Job creation:**
 
 
• Increase in the capital expenditure outlay by 33% to Rs 10 lakh crore, which will create jobs and boost economic growth.
 
• Launch of a new scheme to provide financial assistance to startups and MSMEs.
 
• Extension of the Production Linked Incentive (PLI) scheme to new sectors, such as textiles and food processing.
